solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: C of E tradition is manacling changes

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchy observation that Anglican custom keeps altering the way prisoners are shackled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of England's doctrine and practice as a body of belief is called by this name, after the Anglican communion.

clue.text: Park discovered next to Church Street tube station

indicators.note: discovered means the word park loses its covering outer letters

parts.note: a way is a road or street, as in Broadway

explanation.surface: Directions: a park lies next to the church street by the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCHWAY is a station on London Underground's Northern line.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a stop on the London Underground's Northern line, an example of an Underground station.

clue.text: Scamp is oddly glammy and popular

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions of glammy

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A rascal who is strangely glamorous and well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a cheeky mischievous child much like a scamp.

clue.text: In addition switching wingers leads to foul

indicators.note: wingers are the right and left wings, so one is switched for the other

parts.note: an increment is an addition or increase

explanation.surface: A football report: on top of everything, swapping the wide players brings about a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' are R and L, right and left: INCREMENT has its R swapped for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul weather is stormy, wet and unpleasant, which is the meaning of inclement.

clue.text: The last word from me in a note?

indicators.note: in places the word me within the two letters

explanation.surface: A writer signs off a letter with a final word from themself.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing word of a prayer or hymn, said to end it, is literally the last word.

clue.text: Snub bible lessons having gone in to stop one's humiliation

indicators.note: having gone means those letters leave the word for snub

parts.note: to ignore someone is to snub them
RE, religious education, is the school subject of bible lessons

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so in sits inside the other word

parts.note: my is what one says of one's own things, so one's stands for it

explanation.surface: Cutting religious study by going in to halt one person's embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone' leaves IGNO; 'to stop' is used in the sense of plugging a hole. RE, religious education, is the British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Public shame and disgrace, a deep loss of dignity, is what both words describe.

clue.text: Skinflint's turn of card (Queen)

indicators.note: turn of reverses the kind of card in a phone

parts.note: a SIM card goes in a mobile phone
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A mean player's move in a card game, laying down a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' suggests playing cards but is a SIM card.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending, exactly a skinflint.

clue.text: Miscreant sect holding priest on island

indicators.note: holding means the word for sect contains the other letters

parts.note: a cult is a sect

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the priest above the island

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing religious group detaining a cleric on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person guilty of an offence, a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Redundant description of loch or moisture?

definitions.meaning: Loch Ness, a body of water, could hardly be anything but wet, so describing it as wet is redundant

explanation.surface: A pedant asks whether calling a Scottish lake wet is overstating things.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness, the Scottish lake of monster fame, is wet by nature, so calling it damp says nothing new.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight wetness is the state of being moist, which is moisture.

clue.text: Appear emaciated following cold and cough

indicators.note: following places the thin word after the abbreviation for cold

parts.note: to come is to appear or arrive on the scene
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
lean means thin, emaciated

explanation.surface: Someone shows up gaunt after a cold and a cough, a picture of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cough' looks like part of the illness but is slang for confess, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to cough is to confess, especially to the police; owning up fully means the same.

clue.text: No surprise from Little Stevie?

parts.note: the soul singer Stevie ... began his career billed as Little Stevie ...; a little ... is also the idiom for something unsurprising

explanation.surface: A wry remark that the young Motown star produced nothing unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevie Wonder was billed as 'Little Stevie Wonder' when he started out as a child star at Motown.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means it is hardly surprising, while also naming the singer's early billing as a little Wonder.

clue.text: See 10
One depressive possesses way of talking back that's unseemly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: possesses means the gloomy person holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a moper is a gloomy, depressive person

indicators.note: talking back is read here as the abbreviation running backwards

parts.note: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard British accent, a way of talking

explanation.surface: A gloomy person given to answering back is behaving in an unseemly way.
explanation.walkthrough: Received Pronunciation is the prestige British accent; 'back' gives PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct that falls short of decency or propriety; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Pipe circulating in the ancient expression of celebration

indicators.note: in places the jumbled pipe inside the old form of the article

parts.note: ye is the old way of writing the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

indicators.note: circulating suggests the letters of pipe going round into a new order

explanation.surface: A pipe passed round among the ancients as they celebrate, perhaps a ceremonial smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' looks like passing the pipe round, but it makes IPPE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of delight, the sort of whoop one gives when celebrating good news.

clue.text: First person cuts battered lip and gums boxing

indicators.note: cuts means the pronoun cuts into the jumbled letters
battered says the letters of lip and gums are knocked into a new order

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A fighter's split lip and battered gums are what boxing leaves behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' mixes LIPGUMS as PUGLISM, and I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugilism is the formal word for fighting with fists, the sport of boxing.

clue.text: At this point in pub the start of trouble is to be expected

indicators.note: in puts the word for this place inside the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
here means at this point or place

indicators.note: the start of picks the opening letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: Right here in this pub, trouble is likely to break out, as anyone might predict.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrinsic and built into a thing is naturally bound to occur, so it can be expected.

clue.text: Never mind old, renovated ex-PO van is English and warm

indicators.note: Never mind says to ignore the letter for old
renovated says the letters are made over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An old post office van, done up, is described as English and friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: EXPOVANIS without its O is rearranged as EXPANSIV, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: An expansive person is genial and open, outgoing in manner, much like warm.

clue.text: Memo on the subject of Arthur Daley's employee

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of
in the British TV series Minder, the dodgy dealer Arthur Daley employs Terry as his bodyguard or minder

explanation.surface: A note concerning a character in a British TV crime comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Minder was a British TV comedy-drama in which spiv Arthur Daley employs a bodyguard, his minder.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a written note to jog memory, something that serves to remind.

clue.text: Famous philanthropist almost taken in by regular visitor's success story

indicators.note: taken in by means the shortened name goes inside the word for a visitor

parts.note: a goer is someone who goes regularly, as in churchgoer or theatregoer

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: J. Paul Getty, the oil billionaire, is remembered for the Getty foundations and museum

explanation.surface: A rich benefactor is fooled by a frequent caller who is a self-made success.
explanation.walkthrough: J. Paul Getty, the oil billionaire, founded the Getty museum; 'almost' leaves GETT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambitious, energetic person who strives for and achieves success is described by this hyphenated term.

clue.text: Presented gripping flamboyant dance

indicators.note: gripping means the past tense holds the other letters inside

parts.note: gave means presented
OTT, over the top, means flamboyant or excessive

explanation.surface: A showy, thrilling dance was put on for an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is a French dance of the eighteenth century, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Jerks text resort to the west

indicators.note: to the west places the resort to the left of the text in an across answer

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs
SMS, short message service, is a text message

explanation.surface: Fools send messages about a holiday spot in the west of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden involuntary muscle contractions are jerks or twitches of the body.

clue.text: Crooned about Greek goddess of youth with no energy for affair

indicators.note: about means the past tense of sing goes around the other letters

parts.note: sang means crooned

indicators.note: with no energy drops one E, physics' symbol for energy

parts.note: Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods

explanation.surface: A singer serenades a youthful goddess, but lacks the energy for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no energy' leaves HEB; 'affair' is the informal sense, as in the whole shebang.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a shebang is a matter or affair, as in the whole shebang.

clue.text: Moving vocal, pleasant but lacking energy, is emotionally charged

indicators.note: Moving tells us the letters of vocal shift into a new order
lacking energy drops the E, physics' symbol for energy

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A touching singing performance, agreeable yet flat, still manages to be full of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges VOCAL as VOLCA; NICE without E gives NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, volcanic describes feelings that are fiery and liable to erupt, so heavily charged with emotion.

clue.text: Skill to tie up the French on the ball

indicators.note: to tie up means the word for skill wraps around the other letters

parts.note: art means skill
le is French for the

explanation.surface: It takes skill to bind the French when the ball is at their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alert is quick and attentive, which the idiom of being on the ball also means.

clue.text: 'Peerless' pun I query being peerless

indicators.note: being peerless hints the run of letters stands alone inside the phrase, shorn of the P at its front and the letters at its tail

explanation.surface: A writer queries a pun claiming to be without equal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'pun I query', once the P in front and the RY behind are lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without peer has no equal anywhere, the one and only of its kind.

clue.text: Phoney bellringer denied tricky mood

indicators.note: denied means the letters of mood are refused, taken away from the name
tricky says the letters of mood come in a jumbled order within the name

parts.note: Quasimodo is the bellringer of Notre-Dame in Victor Hugo's novel

explanation.surface: A fake bellringer's awkward temperament is denied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' turns MOOD into MODO, which leaves QUASIMODO.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasi means seeming or apparent but not really so, so it serves as a word for phoney.

clue.text: Pressure on regulars in illegal action

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the pressure letter on top

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

indicators.note: regulars in takes the evenly spaced letters from the word illegal

explanation.surface: Applying pressure to people in an unlawful act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' is meant legally: a plea is a defendant's formal answer in a court action.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a plea is a suit or action brought in court, an old legal sense of the word.

clue.text: Somehow eat ants without an inkling

indicators.note: Somehow says the letters of eat ants are mixed up in some way
without means the letters of an are taken away from the mix

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to consume insects somehow, minus one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: EATANTS less A and N leaves E, T, A, T, S, which 'Somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste of something is a slight hint or small experience of it, much like an inkling.

clue.text: Hype about Andean wool-producer overcoming sloth to become religious leader

indicators.note: about turns the advertising word round

parts.note: ad, short for advertisement, is hype or promotion

indicators.note: overcoming means the animal of the Andes encloses the sloth

parts.note: the llama is a South American animal kept for its wool
the ai is the three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Publicity around a llama defeating a sloth makes it a spiritual figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives DA; the ai, a three-toed sloth, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names the head of Tibetan Buddhism, a religious leader in exile since 1959.

clue.text: Queen Vic hen night tear shed — that's ominous

indicators.note: shed is read as an untidy building, the letters being thrown into disorder
the Queen Vic is the pub in the BBC soap EastEnders, where cockney speech drops the H, so hen becomes en

parts.note: hen as written, before its H is dropped

explanation.surface: At the Queen Vic, a tearful hen party in full swing, which bodes ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Vic is the pub in the London soap EastEnders; cockneys drop their aitches, so HEN loses H. 'shed' mixes ENNIGHTTEAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous things threaten trouble ahead, giving warning that something bad is coming.
